=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- `.github/workflows/comprehensive-test-and-release.yml`:483-490 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: Phase 3 breaks out of the polling loop as soon as a tracking issue is detected, without confirming the orchestrator run completed successfully.
  WHY: The status-failure check runs after the break condition, so a tracking issue can cause the workflow to report success even if the orchestrator later fails; reviewers disagreed on whether this is intended, so the highest severity is kept.
- `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`:941-1004 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The GraphQL test stub uses the issue number to form response keys instead of the query alias, so mocked responses do not match real GraphQL shapes.
  WHY: Production queries key results by aliases like `i0` and `i1`, but the stub returns keys like `i123`, which can hide real lookup failures in code that expects aliased fields.
- `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`:2984-3190 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview]
  PROBLEM: `handle_comprehensive_release_callback_if_needed` still extracts comprehensive-release metadata from tracking-issue comments even though the current workflow no longer emits that metadata path.
  WHY: If the expected marker is absent, the function can derive empty `version_tag`/`test_repo` values and proceed through a dead or manual-only callback path.
- `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`:949-949 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The GraphQL stub redundantly calls `get_issue(num)` twice for the same issue.
  WHY: This is only a minor test-harness inefficiency, but it is still a distinct finding from the alias mismatch.
- `README.md`:1162-1162 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2]
  PROBLEM: The README still describes callback behavior that is no longer reachable through the automated pipeline.
  WHY: The documentation can mislead readers about the current comprehensive-release callback flow.
- `.github/workflows/comprehensive-test-and-release.yml`:142-143,399-400 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview]
  PROBLEM: `jq` parse failures are captured into `BEFORE_IDS_JSON`, which can make error reporting confusing.
  WHY: The workflow exits on parse failure, but the captured stderr text is stored in the same variable as JSON, so the reported payload can contain raw parser errors rather than data.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===
- `.github/workflows/comprehensive-test-and-release.yml`:142-143,399-400 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When `jq` fails to parse `BEFORE_RUNS_JSON`, stderr is captured into `BEFORE_IDS_JSON`, which makes the error message confusing.
  WHY: The workflow prints `BEFORE_IDS_JSON` as if it were JSON, but on parse failure it can contain raw `jq` error text instead of an array.
- `.github/workflows/comprehensive-test-and-release.yml`:440-480 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Phase 3 exits as soon as a tracking issue is detected without waiting to confirm the orchestrator run succeeded.
  WHY: A tracking issue can appear while the orchestrator is still queued or in progress, so the workflow can report success even if the orchestrator later fails.
- `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`:3052-3190 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `handle_comprehensive_release_callback_if_needed` still tries to extract comprehensive-release metadata that the current workflow no longer posts.
  WHY: If the expected metadata marker is missing, the function can produce empty values and call the release workflow with invalid inputs.
- `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`:941-1004 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The GraphQL test stub creates response keys using the issue number rather than the alias used in the query.
  WHY: The mock response shape differs from production GraphQL responses, which can give false confidence in alias-based lookups.
- `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`:949-949 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The GraphQL test stub redundantly calls `get_issue(num)` inside the loop.
  WHY: The issue object is already available earlier, so this is only a minor inefficiency.
- `README.md`:1162-1162 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The README still describes callback behavior that is no longer reachable through the automated pipeline.
  WHY: This documentation mismatch can confuse users even though it does not affect runtime behavior.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===

  WHY: If parsing fails, the variable may contain plain-text `jq` errors, which then makes downstream handling less clear.
- `.github/workflows/comprehensive-test-and-release.yml`:440-480 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Phase 3 can break on tracking-issue detection before confirming the orchestrator finished cleanly.
  WHY: The loop treats issue creation as sufficient evidence of success, so a later orchestrator failure can be masked.
- `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`:941-1004 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The GraphQL test stub stores response fields under keys derived from the issue number instead of the alias.
  WHY: The production query aliases are positional (`i0`, `i1`, etc.), so the stub shape does not match real API responses.
- `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`:2984-3012 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `handle_comprehensive_release_callback_if_needed` remains active even though the trigger path is now inert.
  WHY: The callback depends on metadata that is no longer posted, so the remaining code is dead or manual-only.

=== FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
- `.github/workflows/comprehensive-test-and-release.yml`:483-490 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Phase 3 breaks immediately upon tracking-issue detection, before checking whether the orchestrator run actually succeeded.
  WHY: Because the break happens before the non-success completion check, a completed-but-failed orchestrator run can still leave the workflow reporting success.
- `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`:941-942,1002 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The GraphQL test stub uses the GitHub issue number instead of the query alias when building response keys.
  WHY: Production GraphQL responses use aliases such as `i0` and `i1`, but the stub returns `i<ISSUE_NUMBER>`, which hides alias-based lookup failures.
- `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`:949 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The test stub redundantly calls `get_issue(num)` inside the labels fallback expression.
  WHY: The issue object is already available from the previous line, so the second fetch is unnecessary test-harness overhead.
- `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`:handle_comprehensive_release_callback_if_needed | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Dead callback code remains for a path that is no longer triggered.
  WHY: The label is no longer applied by current workflow automation, so manual activation would reach untested metadata extraction and dispatch behavior.
=== END FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
